title: Yankees’ Aaron Boone admits he fell asleep near end of Knicks’ championship-winning game
content:
TORONTO — New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone had no clue that the New York Knicks had won their first NBA championship in 53 years until Sunday morning.

Boone, a diehard Philadelphia 76ers fan, said he was intently watching Game 5 of the NBA Finals on Saturday night, but he could not stay awake to see the Knicks hoist the Larry O’Brien Championship Trophy and point guard Jalen Brunson named Finals MVP.

“Fell asleep with six minutes to go,” Boone said Sunday morning. “Unbelievable.”

With the Yankees in Canada finishing a three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays, Boone said he was forced to watch the TSN SportsCentre coverage to catch up on what happened at the end of the game. By the time Boone went to sleep, the Knicks had cut the San Antonio Spurs’ lead to four, after trailing by a game-high 16 points.

The Yankees have not won a World Series since 2009, and Boone became the club’s manager in 2018. Seeing a team with significantly less historical success than the Yankees did not let Boone’s mind wander about what it would feel like if his club could win a title under his management.

“I don’t know about that,” Boone said. “There’s such a long way to go in the season. I’ve had the fortune of meeting a handful of those guys over the last few years. I’m really happy for them. Just to see that team, the way they came together and the amazing run they went on in the postseason. That team will be immortalized. Excited for them. Obviously excited for a lot of the people in New York. That’s been a long time coming.”

The Yankees and Knicks, as franchises, have a close relationship. Boone said he became an immediate fan of Brunson when he met the Knicks’ point guard at Yankee Stadium two years ago. The Yankees will also honor Knicks forward Josh Hart, whose great uncle was Elston Howard, with a bobblehead giveaway in late September. Knicks big man Karl-Anthony Towns is also a diehard Yankees fan and threw out a ceremonial first pitch when he was a member of the Minnesota Timberwolves. Yankees captain Aaron Judge also attended Game 4 of the finals — one of the greatest games in sports history — while he continues rehabbing from a rib stress fracture.

But Boone’s heart has always been with the 76ers. His favorite team of all time is the 1983 Sixers, who swept the Los Angeles Lakers in the finals. Inside his Connecticut home, Boone said, are mementos of Moses Malone, Julius Erving, Maurice Cheeks and Andrew Toney, key players on Philadelphia’s title team.

“I know what it means,” Boone said of the feeling New Yorkers are currently experiencing with the Knicks.

Team-building is different in MLB compared to the NBA. But when Boone took over the managerial job after the Yankees lost Game 7 of the American League Championship Series in 2017, it was expected that this franchise would win a title soon. Judge emerged as a superstar, and the Baby Bombers era looked promising. No rational person could have predicted that from that moment until Saturday night, the Knicks, of all teams, would win a title before the Yankees.

But the Knicks reaching the pinnacle was another stark reminder of how far away 2009 feels.
